patterns.name: Express route registered without authentication middleware (TypeScript)
patterns.description: A TypeScript file using Express registers HTTP routes but does not apply authentication middleware. All routes in this file are publicly accessible without authentication. Secure routes with app.use(authMiddleware) globally, or use router-level middleware: router.use(authenticate). Express middleware is applied via use() on the app instance or Router objects. Common patterns: passport.authenticate(), jwt(), requireAuth(), ensureAuthenticated().
patterns.message: File {file} registers Express routes without calling any authentication middleware. {count}/{total} other file(s) in this package use auth. Apply app.use(authMiddleware) or router.use(authMiddleware) before route registration.

patterns.name: Express route registered without rate limiting (TypeScript)
patterns.description: A TypeScript file using Express registers HTTP routes without rate limiting middleware. Routes without rate limiting are vulnerable to credential stuffing, enumeration attacks, and resource exhaustion. Apply rate limiting via app.use(rateLimit({...})) using express-rate-limit or a similar library. Note: if rate limiting is enforced at the infrastructure layer (nginx, load balancer, API gateway, Cloudflare), this finding can be suppressed.
patterns.message: File {file} registers Express routes without rate limiting middleware. {count}/{total} other file(s) in this package apply rate limiting. Add express-rate-limit via app.use(rateLimit({...})) or apply at the infrastructure layer.

patterns.name: Express POST/mutation route without CSRF protection (TypeScript)
patterns.description: A TypeScript file using Express registers POST, PUT, DELETE, or PATCH routes without CSRF protection middleware. CSRF protection is required for web applications that use session cookies for authentication. If this is a JSON API using token-based auth (JWT, Bearer), CSRF protection is not needed and this finding can be suppressed. Use csurf, csrf-csrf (doubleCsrfProtection), or lusca for CSRF protection.
patterns.message: File {file} registers Express mutation routes (POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH) without CSRF protection. {count}/{total} other file(s) in this package use CSRF protection. Apply csrf protection via app.use(csrfProtection()) or suppress if using token-based auth.

patterns.name: Fastify route registered without authentication (TypeScript)
patterns.description: A TypeScript file using Fastify registers HTTP routes but does not apply authentication. All routes in this file are publicly accessible without authentication. Secure routes using Fastify hooks: fastify.addHook('preHandler', async (request) => { await request.jwtVerify() }) globally or per-route. Register auth plugins via fastify.register(fastifyJWT, { secret }) or fastify.register(fastifyAuth). The jwtVerify() method from @fastify/jwt is the canonical Fastify JWT auth pattern.
patterns.message: File {file} registers Fastify routes without authentication. {count}/{total} other file(s) in this package use auth. Apply fastify.addHook('preHandler', authenticate) globally or use request.jwtVerify() per-route.

patterns.name: Next.js API route handler without authentication (TypeScript)
patterns.description: A Next.js API route handler file does not call any authentication function. In Next.js App Router, route.ts files export GET/POST handlers that execute server-side — they must validate the caller's identity explicitly. In Pages Router, pages/api/*.ts handlers are similarly unprotected. Auth can be handled via: getServerSession() from next-auth, auth() from Auth.js v5, currentUser() from Clerk, or a custom authenticate() function. Note: if auth is enforced globally via middleware.ts using withAuth or similar, this per-route finding can be suppressed. Note: no framework_identifiers gate is used — the route.ts and pages/api/*.ts file naming conventions are Next.js-specific, so the handler_file_patterns alone are sufficient and avoid false negatives on minimal handlers with no next/* imports.
patterns.message: Next.js API route {file} does not call any authentication function. Use getServerSession(), auth(), currentUser(), or a custom authenticate() to verify caller identity. Suppress if auth is enforced globally via middleware.ts.

patterns.name: Next.js API route handler without rate limiting (TypeScript)
patterns.description: A Next.js API route handler (TypeScript) does not apply rate limiting. App Router route.ts files and Pages Router pages/api/*.ts handlers are exposed to the internet and are vulnerable to credential stuffing, enumeration attacks, and resource exhaustion without rate limiting. The primary pattern is per-route rate limiting via @upstash/ratelimit: import { Ratelimit } from '@upstash/ratelimit' and call ratelimit.limit() in the handler. Alternative libraries: next-rate-limit, express-rate-limit (via custom wrappers), or infrastructure-level limiting (Cloudflare, AWS WAF). Note: if rate limiting is enforced globally at the infrastructure layer for Vercel-deployed projects or via a CDN/load balancer, this per-route finding can be suppressed. Note: no framework_identifiers gate is used — the route.ts and pages/api/*.ts file naming conventions are Next.js-specific, so the handler_file_patterns alone are sufficient and avoid false negatives on minimal handlers with no next/* imports.
patterns.message: Next.js API route {file} does not apply rate limiting. Apply per-route rate limiting via @upstash/ratelimit or a similar library. Suppress if rate limiting is enforced at the infrastructure layer (Vercel, Cloudflare, AWS WAF, or similar).

patterns.name: TypeScript route or controller directly imports database package
patterns.description: A TypeScript file in the route, controller, or API handler layer directly imports a database package instead of going through a repository or service layer. This couples the HTTP layer directly to data storage, making the code harder to test, refactor, and secure. Access data through a dedicated service or repository layer.
patterns.message: File {file} appears to be a route/controller but directly imports database package '{target}'. Access data through a repository or service layer instead.
